title: Gaurī lowed, shaping the waters

words.context: Sāyaṇa: «माध्यमिका वाक्», the speech of the middle region (thunder); others read her as speech itself

words.role: first of the series describing her

samasa.meaning: she who has a thousand syllables
she who has one foot (or one step, one station)

morphology.note: locative singular without the ending -i, a Vedic form (later व्योम्नि).
feminine of the perfect participle babhūvas, ‘having become’.
the Ṛgveda (1.164.41) reads गौरीः, with -s, which Sāyaṇa explains as a Vedic nominative («सुलोपाभावश्छान्दसः»); the Brāhmaṇa reads गौरी.

translation.literal: Gaurī lowed, shaping the waters: one-footed, two-footed, she four-footed, eight-footed, nine-footed having become, of a thousand syllables in the highest heaven.
translation.readable: The bright cow lowed and shaped the waters. She became one-footed, two-footed, four-footed, eight-footed, nine-footed — a thousand syllables in the highest heaven.

meaning: A riddle-verse from the long hymn of Dīrghatamas (RV 1.164.41), also in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa (2.4.6). A cow, Gaurī, lows and shapes the waters; she grows from one foot to two, four, eight and nine, and becomes a thousand syllables in the highest heaven. Sāyaṇa reads her first as the thunder, the speech of the middle region, whose sound brings the rain and spreads to the quarters of the sky; then, with others, as speech itself, which names and so makes things, and grows from a single undivided sound into countless words. The verse addresses neither Soma nor a graha: it praises Gaurī, speech.
in_the_rite: The third mantra of Soma’s step in the Navagraha sūktam (witness S), after āpyāyasva and apsu me. S names the adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together, so the edition does not say which this verse is for; the verse itself praises Gaurī. Its use for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa, on the Ṛgveda, takes Gaurī first as the thunder: «माध्यमिका वाक्», the speech of the middle region; the waters are rain, and the feet are her stations — one in the cloud, two with the sky, four with the quarters, eight with the intermediate quarters, nine with the zenith. ‘A thousand syllables’ means without measure: «अपरिमितव्याप्तियुक्ता». He adds a second reading, ‘some say’: Gaurī is speech as the Word-Brahman, «शब्दब्रह्मात्मिका वाक्».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: The four lines are not the four pādas of the Ṛgveda verse (a jagatī/triṣṭubh) but the Brāhmaṇa’s division of it into short phrases, as the base witness prints them.

notes.label: historical
notes.text: RV 1.164.41 reads गौरीर्मिमाय; the Brāhmaṇa and this recitation read गौरी मिमाय.
